$comment: Hostile strings for e2e/pro-xss.spec.ts. One place to review every payload the
browser tests push through the cookie scanner's rendering path.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. tests/xss-protection.test.ts and
scripts/security/checks/sast-dynamic-code-sinks.mjs read the SOURCE and assert
that no component hands scan data to dangerouslySetInnerHTML. That is a real
guard, but it cannot say what a RUNNING page does with a hostile value: React
escaping, a stray title=, an href, a third-party widget, or a future refactor
are all outside a grep's reach. pro-xss.spec.ts renders these payloads in a
real Chromium and checks the DOM that came out.
THE MARKER. Every payload tries to reach `window.__xss`. Two shapes are used:
- `window.__xss=1`, wherever an `=` is legal in the sink;
- `__xssFlag()`, a function the spec installs with addInitScript, for sinks
where an `=` would be eaten before it ever reaches the renderer (a cookie
NAME: document.cookie and lib parseCookieList both split a name on `=`).
Either one setting window.__xss is a failure.
EXPECTED TEXT. `expect` lists the substrings that MUST still be readable in the
result panel after rendering. The full literal, angle brackets and all, is the
discriminator: if a payload were injected as markup instead of escaped, the
element's textContent would hold the tag's inner text and NOT `<script>`/`<img`.
Silently dropping the value is a failure too — this tool is an audit, and an
auditor who cannot see the hostile cookie name cannot report it.
WHERE `expect` IS SPLIT. The Paste box's parser (components/tools/
CookieAnalyzerTool.tsx parseCookieList) splits input on `[;\n]` and then on the
first `=`, so one pasted payload legitimately lands in several elements. Those
entries list the pieces, not the whole string.

scan.$comment: Fields of the /api/scan-url response body. The spec fulfils the request with page.route() — no real scan, no load on the droplet. Sink line numbers are components/tools/CookieAnalyzerTool.tsx as of 2026-09-21.

url.sink:
line 642 —

{urlResult.url}

, and urlScanReport() feeds new URL(url).hostname into the result-card headline

cookieSameSite.sink: line 764 — SameSite: {c.sameSite} (the value is also .toLowerCase()'d to pick a colour)

paste.$comment: Typed straight into the Paste textarea. No network at all — parseCookieList runs in the page. Split expectations are the parser's doing, not a sanitiser's.

quoteBreakout.note: parseCookieList splits on ';' then on the first '=': piece 1 is the cookie named '"', piece 2 becomes name '<script>window.__xss' with value '1</script>'.

multiline.sink: lines 843/856 — {c.name} and {c.value}, one row per line
multiline.note: Line 2 splits into name '">'. Line 3 carries no '=' so the whole tag stays the cookie name. Line 4 keeps the whole tag as the value.

thisPage.$comment: Written with document.cookie before clicking Scan Cookies, so the payload arrives the way a hostile first-party cookie really would. Chromium's cookie parser was checked empirically: it keeps < > " / and spaces, and treats the FIRST '=' as the name/value separator — hence the name payload carries no '='.
